blocker.statement: No uncontaminated SecHelix run exists yet. The 38-fixture / 76-case suite was authored and expanded by assistant sessions working inside this repository, including the sessions that would have acted as the evaluated model. Those sessions know the fixtures, the pairings and the rationales, so scoring one of them would measure recall of authored answers rather than security-review capability. The disqualification is deliberately broad: any session that has read evals/fixtures/, scripts/build_eval_fixtures.py, or gold-packs/*/pack.json is excluded, because partial knowledge of a paired suite still leaks the answer to its twin.
what_would_unblock_it: A run by a model or session that has not read evals/fixtures/, scripts/build_eval_fixtures.py, or gold-packs/*/pack.json.
Copy evals/blind-packet/cases.json out of this repository and evaluate it in an isolated session.
Produce a prediction packet with every field of the run record populated.
Score with: python evals/run_evals.py --predictions work/predictions.json --output work/result.json
Publish only if sechelix_commit, agent_host, model and limitations are all present.
blocker.packet_ready: evals/blind-packet/ — 76 blind cases with exact run instructions

fixture_suite.note: Counts describe the available suite; they are not a measurement. `families` is the number of distinct free-text `family` labels carried by the fixtures, which is what the per-family breakdown is keyed on. `family_ids` lists the catalog family segments that appear in the fixture IDs (EVAL-<FAMILY>-<n>); there are more of those than there are labels, because AUTH and SESS fixtures share one label.
